title: South Alabama football opens fall camp practice - NewsBreak
text:
By Gerhard Mathangani Gabriella Genereaux ,
1 hours ago
MOBILE, Ala. (WKRG) — South Alabama began preparations for the 2026 season with the first day of fall camp practice on Wednesday. Head coach Major Applewhite enters his third season at the helm. The Jags added 27 new players and a few additions to the coaching staff. Todd Orlando takes over as defensive coordinator and former quarterback Tim Rattay is the team’s new passing game coordinator.
“I think the first thing we got to get changed is the run game from last year,” Orlando said.
“For people to be able to take the ball and just run it on us. That’s they’re not going to win a lot of ball games that way. So establish the fundamentals and technical part of it, toughen up – that’s the big part – and then play explosive on defense.”
Applewhite wants competition at every position to ensure depth for the long season.
“We’re going to compete at every position. Quarterback is one of the 22 we’re going to compete at on offense and defense,” Applewhite said. “All of our specialist jobs are open. All of our punter jobs are open. At the end of the day, just having played that position, it doesn’t matter whether you’re in the SEC or the Sun Belt, you better have two ready.”
South Alabama will host Southeastern Louisiana in the season opener on September 5 at Hancock Whitney Stadium.
